title: Umbwe Route · 6 days
content:
This trek offers an adventurous ascent up Mount Kilimanjaro via the challenging Umbwe Route, known for its steep and direct approach. Starting from the southern side of the mountain, this route provides a dramatic and less-traveled path to the summit. Upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, you will be welcomed by our driver and transferred to the Hotel for a comfortable night, including a pre-trek briefing with your guides.

The trek begins at the Umbwe Gate, where you will traverse through dense forests and ascend through rugged terrain, eventually reaching the high-altitude zones. You will acclimate at various camps, ensuring a safe and steady ascent. After reaching Uhuru Peak, you’ll descend through lush rainforests to the Mweka Gate. Completing the trek, you will return to the Hotel for rest and reflection. For those looking to extend their adventure, options for a safari or a beach vacation in Zanzibar are available.

This overview captures the essence of the Umbwe Route, emphasizing its unique challenges and the stunning natural beauty that awaits trekkers.

faqs.title: How long does it take to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: The duration of a Kilimanjaro climb typically ranges from 5 to 10 days, depending on the chosen route and your acclimatization needs. Longer treks allow for better acclimatization and increase the chances of reaching the summit.

faqs.title: What is the best time to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: The best times to climb are during the dry seasons, which run from late June to October and from mid-January to March. These months generally offer clearer skies and better weather conditions.

faqs.title: Do I need to be an experienced climber to summit Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: No previous climbing experience is necessary to summit Kilimanjaro. However, a good level of physical fitness, preparation, and understanding of altitude sickness are important for a successful climb.

faqs.title: What are the different routes to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: There are several routes to summit Kilimanjaro, including the Marangu, Machame, Lemosho, and Rongai routes. Each varies in difficulty, scenery, and duration, so choose one that aligns with your preferences and fitness level.

faqs.title: What should I pack for climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Essential gear includes layered clothing, a waterproof jacket, sturdy hiking boots, a sleeping bag rated for cold temperatures, trekking poles, a headlamp, and personal items like sunscreen, a hat, and a water bottle. Consult your tour operator for a comprehensive packing list.

faqs.title: How high is Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Mount Kilimanjaro stands at approximately 5,895 meters (19,341 feet) above sea level, making it the highest peak in Africa.

faqs.title: What is altitude sickness, and how can I prevent it?
faqs.content: Altitude sickness occurs when your body struggles to acclimatize to high elevations, leading to symptoms like headache, nausea, and fatigue. To minimize the risk, ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and consider taking a medication like Diamox. Listen to your body and communicate with your guides.

faqs.title: Are there age restrictions for climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Yes, climbers must be at least 10 years old to trek Kilimanjaro, and those under 18 should be accompanied by an adult. Some operators have specific age limits, so check with your chosen tour company.

faqs.title: Will I need a guide to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Yes, all climbers are required to go with a licensed guide and a support team. This is essential for safety, navigation, and to comply with Tanzanian regulations.

faqs.title: What is the success rate for reaching the summit?
faqs.content: Success rates vary by route, but generally hover around 50-65% for shorter treks. Longer routes that allow for better acclimatization tend to have higher success rates, often exceeding 80%.

faqs.title: Is there a chance of communication during the climb?
faqs.content: You may have limited cell phone coverage on certain routes, but it’s advisable to expect minimal connectivity. Most trekkers focus on enjoying the experience and the beautiful surroundings rather than staying connected.

itinerary.title: Day 1
itinerary.content:
As you arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport, our dedicated driver will be eagerly anticipating your arrival, holding a sign with your name for a warm welcome. You’ll enjoy a seamless transfer to the Hotel, where a delicious meal awaits you.

Later, our experienced mountain coordinators and your guide will provide a pre-trekking briefing, offering insights into the wonders that await during your expedition. Take advantage of the relaxing environment at Hotel, which features a swimming pool, beautiful gardens, a bar, and a restaurant, ensuring a comfortable start to your adventure.

Overnight: Sal salinero hotel or similar

itinerary.title: Day 2
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 1,800 meters (5,906 feet) – 2,850 meters (9,350 feet)
  • Hiking distance: 11 km
  • Hiking time: 6 to 7 hours

After breakfast, you’ll be transferred to the Umbwe Gate to begin your trek. The path through the dense rainforest is steep and demanding, providing a true wilderness experience. As you gradually ascend, you’ll witness the rich vegetation and unique atmosphere of the rainforest, filled with vibrant flora and the sounds of nature.

Upon reaching Umbwe Camp, you can enjoy a hot meal prepared by our chef, giving you the energy needed for the days ahead. This initial section of the trek, while challenging, sets the stage for the adventures to come. Settle in for the night at the camp, nestled in the lush forest, where you can relax and rejuvenate for the next day’s journey.

itinerary.title: Day 3
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 2,850 meters (9,350 feet) – 3,960 meters (13,000 feet)
  • Hiking distance: 6 km
  • Hiking time: 6 to 7 hours

After enjoying breakfast at Machame Camp, you’ll set off towards Shira Camp, covering about 5 kilometers in a journey that typically takes 4 to 5 hours.

The trail begins with a steep ascent through the scenic moorland zone, where you’ll be treated to breathtaking views as you climb. As you near Shira Camp, you’ll walk along a ridge offering spectacular vistas of the surrounding landscape. Upon arrival, the porters will set up your tents and prepare lunch. You’ll have the afternoon to relax and acclimate to the altitude before dinner, followed by a briefing from your guide on the next day’s trek.

itinerary.title: Day 4
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 3,960 m – 4,035 m
  • Hiking distance: 5 km
  • Hiking time: 5 hours

Start your day early with a wake-up call and a nourishing breakfast to fuel your trek. The journey may involve ascending the famous Barranco Wall, a steep but rewarding section that offers stunning views once conquered. After navigating the Wall, you’ll descend into the scenic Karanga Valley, renowned for its lush vegetation and breathtaking landscapes.

Upon reaching the Karanga campsite, the porters will set up tents while our chef prepares lunch. After your meal, you’ll embark on an acclimatization hike towards Barafu Camp, ascending 200 meters before returning to camp. In the evening, enjoy a hot meal prepared by the chef. Following dinner, your experienced guide will brief you on the next day’s trek, discussing the route, challenges, and key details.

itinerary.title: Day 5
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 4,035 m – 4,640 m
  • Hiking distance: 5 km
  • Hiking time: 5 hours

Start your day with an early wake-up call and a hearty breakfast to fuel your trek toward Barafu Camp. The trail features varied terrain, including rocky sections and gradual slopes, offering breathtaking views of Kilimanjaro’s high-altitude landscapes. As you ascend, focus on acclimatization to avoid altitude-related issues.

Upon reaching Barafu Camp, our porters will handle camp setup while the chef prepares lunch. After eating, take the opportunity to rest until dinner. In the evening, your guide will brief you on the upcoming summit attempt, covering the route, challenges, safety measures, and preparations. Be sure to rest well, as the summit ascent begins late in the evening.

itinerary.title: Day 6
itinerary.desc: Barafu Camp to Uhuru Peak and Mweka Camp
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 4,640 m – 5, 895 m – 3,090 m
  • Hiking distance: 17 km
  • Hiking & descending time: 15+ hours

You’ll rise around 11:30 PM and start the ascent after having some tea and biscuits. Heading northwest, you’ll climb through scree towards Stella Point on the crater rim. The trek to Stella Point (5,685 m) takes about 6 hours and is often the most mentally and physically challenging part of the climb.

After a brief rest at Stella Point, you’ll be rewarded with a magnificent sunrise, weather permitting. From there, it’s a 2-hour ascent to Uhuru Peak, the highest point on Mount Kilimanjaro. Your time at the summit will depend on the weather, so don’t linger too long due to the cold and fatigue.

The descent to Barafu Camp takes about 3 hours for a short rest before continuing to Mweka Camp, where you’ll enjoy dinner and overnight accommodations. This day is both challenging and rewarding, offering stunning views and a sense of accomplishment at reaching the summit.

itinerary.title: Day 7
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 3,090 m – 1,650 m
  • Hiking distance: 10 km
  • Descending time: 4-5 hours

After breakfast at Mweka Camp, you’ll begin your descent to Mweka Gate, where you’ll complete the final leg of your trek. Upon reaching the gate, you’ll be driven back to your Hotel, where a hot lunch and a refreshing shower await you.

At the end of the trip, tipping the team is encouraged and appreciated; special envelopes for this purpose are available at the hotel. If you wish to extend your adventure with a safari, you can meet with our safari coordinator at the hotel. After some rest, the coordinator will provide a briefing on the various safari options available. We highly recommend booking a safari with us to experience Tanzania’s stunning wildlife and natural beauty, making your journey truly unforgettable.

Overnight: Sal salinero hotel or similar

itinerary.title: Day 8
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, you’ll be transferred back to Kilimanjaro International Airport for your departure. If you’re looking to extend your adventure, consider adding a day trip to your itinerary to explore nearby attractions or immerse yourself in the local culture. For more details, visit our Day Trip page.

Alternatively, you might want to continue your journey with a visit to the stunning island of Zanzibar. Whether you seek relaxation on pristine beaches or wish to delve into the island’s rich culture, Zanzibar offers something for everyone. Explore our Zanzibar page to discover the perfect package for your next excursion.

If you’re interested in adding a safari experience, please visit our Safari page for more information on our exciting safari options.
